answer: Submissions that land within 298 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The nadir detector writes to whisper, and garden reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 42 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
